saw_lines: Recruiters rarely switch sourcing tools over a feature list. They test one live search, then switch if it finds new people.
So the sale is won in the first line, and your ads give no number or offer to answer the question.
Your 19 live ads, 0 with a proof number, leave a recruiter nothing to weigh the tool against. Pull one real count and open the next three ads with it.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 13 Nov 2026
points: 0 of 19 ads carry a proof number, so a recruiter has nothing to weigh the tool against before clicking. Next move: pull one real count, like searches run, and open the next three ads with it.
0 of 19 ads mention an offer or discount, so a new buyer has no reason to act today. Next move: bundle a guided first search as a first order offer, and open three new ads with it.

Your 19 ads open with 18 different stories, so no angle is repeated enough. The one you already repeat most, replace your old sourcing tool, leads 2 ads. Next move: keep that story and build three variations from it.

Your ads use Learn more on 15, See details on 3 and Sign up on 1, so the button rarely matches the promise. Next move: one button per angle that names the payoff, like Read the story for case studies.
